description: A principal must decide whether to authorize converting an unused courtyard into a science learning garden and finalize the site's preparation, plant design, instructional use, and maintenance plan, with input from the facilities manager and the science teacher.

shared_context.S1: The school has an unused paved courtyard that a proposal would convert into a science learning garden.
shared_context.S2: The proposal currently calls for planting six species directly in the existing soil, beginning in September, with three science lessons held in the garden.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Morgan must approve the conversion and its operating plan before any work begins.
shared_context.S4: As part of the school's normal facilities-and-curriculum pre-approval review, Dr. Morgan asks the facilities manager and science teacher to report anything that should be included before the decision is finalized.

PF1.text: A soil laboratory report that Ms. Shah received yesterday found lead at 185 parts per million in the courtyard soil, above the district's 100-parts-per-million threshold; district procedure therefore requires removing the top 8 inches and replacing it with certified clean soil before students use the garden. The report is still in the facilities folder awaiting the weekly review and has not been added to the project proposal.

PF2.text: The science department's executed garden-learning grant requires the project to include exactly 10 native plant species, provide exactly 6 science lessons in the garden by November 1, 2026, and schedule supervised maintenance on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 2:30 p.m.; Mr. Ellis received the grant terms from the department office this week, but the proposal was drafted before the award was finalized.

acceptance_conditions: The courtyard conversion must be approved.
The contaminated top 8 inches of soil must be removed.
Replacement soil must be certified clean.
The garden must contain exactly 10 native plant species.
Exactly 6 science lessons must be scheduled in the garden by November 1, 2026.
Supervised maintenance must be scheduled on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 2:30 p.m.
A formal soil-remediation record must be committed.
A formal grant-compliance record must be committed.
The soil laboratory finding must be cited by the decision-maker after it is spoken aloud.

decisive_facts.why: The soil report changes preparation from planting in existing soil to removing exactly 8 inches and replacing it with certified clean soil, and it creates the need for a formal soil-remediation record.

The executed grant changes the design to exactly 10 native species, changes instruction to exactly 6 garden lessons completed by November 1, 2026, changes maintenance to Tuesdays and Thursdays at 2:30 p.m., and requires a grant-compliance record.
